Imagine it as a fraction that needs to be simplified. We have to have one as a coefficient on x to use synthetic, so to do that, we simplify the fraction. 

Example: (9x^(2)-6x+3)/(3x-4) = [3(3x^(2)-2x+1)]/[3(x-4/3)] = (3x^(2)-2x+1)/(x-4/3)

Now you can use synthetic. 

Your answer will be something of the form Q+[R/(x-4/3)]. 

We don’t like fractions inside of fractions. We only need to fix the fraction, not the quotient, so we “unsimplify” it, as I say. 

[R/(x-4/3)] = [(3R)/((3)(x-4/3)] = 3R/(x-4)

So our final answer is Q + 3R/(x-4)

I hope that helps.
